rv.q: There were opportunities here to craft either a tighter thriller or a more penetrating character study; Street opts for something in-between, light on dramatic momentum but rich in biographical detail.
A Small And Quiet Light, Stephanie Street's warm, theatrical tribute to Khan, is so anxious to be respectful, it makes our heroine seem a little dull.
Unfortunately, this play managed neither for me.

cn.t: Critics find this WWII drama about heroic agent Noor Inayat Khan well-intentioned but dramatically inert, with a meandering structure and overly reverent approach that fails to do justice to its fascinating, underrepresented subject.
